title: Functions, Lambdas & Comprehensions
intro: Python functions interview questions for freshers go beyond def and return — interviewers want to know if you understand how Python passes arguments, what *args and **kwargs actually do, and whether you can write Pythonic code instead of Java-with-Python-syntax. This page covers default argument values and the mutable default argument trap (the most common Python gotcha in fresher interviews), *args and **kwargs (how they capture positional and keyword arguments respectively), lambda as anonymous single-expression functions, map() and filter() as functional alternatives to for-loops, list/dict/set comprehensions as the idiomatic Python pattern for building new collections, and a first look at decorators at the concept level — what they do (wrap a function to add behaviour) without the full advanced decorator protocol.
